neighbours.label: The adverb 'all' opening a stretch of distance or time right after a verb or preposition ('all the way to/back to', 'all over the world', 'all across', 'all along', 'all night'), peaking on 'all' itself; quiet for determiner 'all' before a noun, for 'all alone', for 'it was all over' meaning finished, and for the same stretch said without 'all' ('throughout', 'the whole way', 'across'). Known leak: the verb 'work' in 'work your way up/through'.
fire: We drove all the way to the coast without stopping once.
She walked all the way back to the station in the rain.
Fans traveled from all over the world to see the final.
The news spread all across the country within hours.
I knew all along that the key was in my coat pocket.
The baby cried all night, so nobody got any sleep.
He ran all the way home after school.
Wildflowers bloomed all along the riverbank this spring.
quiet: He gave all his savings to charity.
The old dog sat all alone by the door.
We drove the whole way to the coast without stopping once.
She walked back to the station in the rain.
Fans traveled from around the world to see the final.
The news spread across the country within hours.
I suspected from the start that the key was in my coat pocket.
The baby cried throughout the night, so nobody got any sleep.
